features.description: Introduce operator_surface as a first-class typed axis and a four-axis InvocationContext (operator_surface x agent_runtime x role x execution_locality), reusing agent_surface for the runtime axis and existing ROLES for worker roles. execution_locality is a sharp enum, not a thin local|remote, so the Cowork-VM-vs-Mac-code-task distinction is representable. New engine module; no parallel runtime/capability registry.
features.acceptance: A pure module defines an OperatorSurface enum (at minimum terminal, dashboard, codex_app, claude_desktop, claude_dispatch, antigravity, cursor, github_agent_hq, remote_vm, unknown), an ExecutionLocality enum (exactly local_mac, plan_worktree, dashboard_terminal, code_task, remote_vm, github_vm, unknown), and an InvocationContext dataclass with exactly the fields operator_surface, agent_runtime, role, execution_locality. agent_runtime values validate against the SAME source as agent_surface (unknown agents map to unknown_runtime, not an invented registry entry). Serialization round-trips byte-stable (no timestamps) and a test asserts no field name contains _token/_key/_secret and that every enum member round-trips.

features.description: Resolve an InvocationContext explicit-first, heuristic-second, unknown-last. Explicit env vars override everything; documented process/env heuristics fill gaps; anything unresolved becomes an explicit unknown_* member rather than a guess. Pure resolver; reuses the execution_environment.py env-plumbing pattern.
features.acceptance: resolve_context(env, *, repo, plan) returns an InvocationContext where: (1) DONT_PANIC_OPERATOR / DONT_PANIC_AGENT / DONT_PANIC_ROLE / DONT_PANIC_LOCALITY when set are honored verbatim and beat all heuristics; (2) with no explicit vars, documented heuristics (at least TERM_PROGRAM -> operator_surface, a known agent env marker -> agent_runtime) populate fields; (3) any unresolved field is set to the axis's unknown_* member, never a most-likely guess (an unrecognized TERM_PROGRAM yields unknown, not a wrong surface); (4) the function is pure (no I/O, no mutation of the passed env). Tests cover explicit-wins, each heuristic, and unknown-fallback.

features.description: Record every DontPanic CLI invocation to a sanitized, concurrency-safe presence ledger. Each record carries the four-axis context plus repo/worktree/branch/plan, the command, started_at/finished_at/last_seen, result, and locality. Hardened for multiple simultaneous agents: atomic/locked append, command-string argument redaction (not just field-name checks), no raw home paths, and a retention/compaction policy.
features.acceptance: Running any dontpanic subcommand appends exactly one InvocationRecord to ~/.dontpanic/invocations.jsonl (path via global_config.dontpanic_home, redirectable by the test env so the suite never writes the real home). Each record contains the four-axis context (F001), repo + worktree + branch + plan (or null), command, started_at, finished_at, last_seen, result (ok|error|interrupted), and locality. Writing is wired at ONE seam in cli.py and is (a) atomic/lock-safe: a concurrency test issuing N simultaneous appends yields N well-formed lines with no interleaving/corruption; (b) sanitized: a token-shaped argument in the command string is redacted, and no absolute home path appears (asserted by test); (c) bounded: a documented retention/compaction step caps the ledger (test shows old records compacted). result=error is recorded for a failing command.

features.description: Operator-role PREFERENCES config layer (intent) — an easy CLI to set and list operator roles ('Claude primary_operator, Codex auditor, Gemini researcher, Cursor as primary_operator'), stored under a distinct config namespace operator_roles.* that is SEPARATE from the worker role namespace and carries NO assert_registrable guard, so non-executor surfaces (e.g. cursor) can be a preferred operator. Config-write mechanics only; the read-only projection and the dispatch boundary are owned by their own features.
features.acceptance: An OPERATOR_ROLES set (at minimum primary_operator, researcher, reviewer, designer, tester, release_operator) is defined distinct from agent_surface.ROLES. An easy CLI sets and lists them, writing operator_roles.<role> = <name> to a distinct config key (global default, project-scoped optional) WITHOUT invoking assert_registrable (a non-executor surface like cursor is accepted). A test asserts: (1) setting an operator role writes only the operator_roles.* config key, never the worker role namespace, and never refuses a non-executor; (2) list returns the resolved operator-role map. No conflation between the two role namespaces.

features.description: Read-only dashboard operator-role matrix projection. A pure projection renders the operator_roles.* preferences as a role matrix consumed by the dashboard, shown SEPARATELY from the worker-dispatch roles so the two namespaces never conflate in the rendered view. Projection only — no mutation, no dispatch semantics.
features.acceptance: A pure projection renders the operator-role matrix consumed by the dashboard from the operator_roles config (F004). A test asserts: (1) the projection is pure (derived from operator_roles, no I/O and no mutation of inputs); (2) it returns/renders the resolved operator-role map; (3) operator-role PREFERENCES are rendered distinctly from worker roles.* (no conflation of the two namespaces in the matrix). The projection surfaces preferences as intent only and carries no dispatchability claim.

features.description: Dispatch-safety guard for the SAFETY INVARIANT (D009): operator_roles.* express preference/intent ONLY and are NEVER dispatch authorization. Assigning a surface/agent an operator role must never make DontPanic able to spawn it as a worker. Dispatch authority derives SOLELY from executors/AGENT_REGISTRY via the worker roles.* namespace. This feature pins that boundary in the dispatch path and proves it.
features.acceptance: SAFETY INVARIANT test: setting operator_roles.primary_operator = cursor (a non-executor) does NOT make cursor appear in worker-dispatch resolution and does NOT make it dispatchable — dispatch authority derives SOLELY from executors/AGENT_REGISTRY via the worker roles.* namespace, so dispatching a surface that holds only an operator-role preference is refused exactly as if no role were set. A preference-only surface is refused at dispatch. A test asserts no operator_roles read path can grant or widen dispatchability, and that the worker register-worker / assert_registrable path is unchanged by the presence of operator-role preferences.

features.description: Channel doctor CLI: dontpanic doctor --channel <surface> (alias --operator-surface) reuses the existing doctor_registry + capability verify.probes to report whether a named operator surface is usable. Consumes the operator-surface capability-manifest kind from F008; introduces no agent-channels.json.
features.acceptance: dontpanic doctor --channel <surface> (and alias --operator-surface) resolves that surface's operator-surface capability manifest (F008) and runs its probes via doctor_registry, reporting PATH / home / repo visibility / worktree-binding / config / MCP availability with pass/warn/fail per check; an unknown surface name exits non-zero with an actionable message; no agent-channels.json file is introduced (asserted by test). The doctor remains non-blocking/structural-safe when run with --skip-auth.

features.description: Operator-surface capability-manifest shape. Extend the EXISTING capability schema with an operator-surface/runtime manifest kind (no parallel agent-channels.json) and seed manifests for real surfaces (e.g. cursor, claude_desktop, codex_app, antigravity) so named surfaces are actually supportable, not just enumerated.
features.acceptance: The capability schema accepts a new kind for operator surfaces/runtimes (e.g. operator_surface) with the fields doctor needs (verify.probes, requires, owner_boundary), and at least two seeded manifests for real surfaces are added under capabilities/. A test asserts no agent-channels.json file is introduced.

features.description: Channel-view producer + pure JS logic module. A build-time producer derives a channel-view object ONLY from the invocation ledger (F003) + capabilities incl. operator-surface manifests (F008) + worktree bindings + operator_roles (F004) and emits it as dashboard state JSON alongside operator-triage.json (no new registry). A pure JS logic module derives the panel buckets + operator-role matrix. Conflict/health semantics go beyond same-plan to worktree-binding health and dispatchability.
features.acceptance: A producer builds a channel-view object derived ONLY from the ledger + capabilities/*.json (incl. operator-surface manifests) + worktree bindings + operator_roles; a test asserts NO agent-channels.json is introduced and that supports_* / dispatchability for a known runtime derive from capabilities + AGENT_REGISTRY, not hardcoded. A pure JS logic module derives panel buckets active, stale, remote_only, same_plan_conflict, same_branch, same_repo, unhealthy_worktree_binding, remote_cannot_mutate_local, operator_only_runtime_not_dispatchable, plus the operator-role matrix, with vitest unit tests per bucket (including same-plan and operator-only-not-dispatchable).

features.description: Dashboard 'Operator Channels' panel. Renders the buckets and operator-role matrix derived by F009, following the operator-triage/v0 producer<->render boundary, read-only. Enters through the real surface: real producer -> real shell journey + a Python fixture<->producer contract test.
features.acceptance: The panel renders all active and needs-attention items uncapped across the F009 buckets (active, stale, remote_only, same_plan_conflict, same_branch, same_repo, unhealthy_worktree_binding, remote_cannot_mutate_local, operator_only_runtime_not_dispatchable) plus the operator-role matrix. A real-state journey test boots the dashboard shell against a real producer-emitted fixture (not a hand-authored synthetic) and a Python fixture<->producer contract test guards the producer/consumer shape (QA-sufficiency contract).
